items.title: Stephanie Vaquer Cleared To Face Becky Lynch On Raw
items.summary: Stephanie Vaquer announced on social media that she has been medically cleared, dramatically discarding her crutches. She confirmed she will meet Becky Lynch on Monday's WWE Raw, following a confrontation in the trainer's room where Adam Pearce said the two would face off once Vaquer was ready. Vaquer's most recent match was a triple threat at WWE Money in the Bank against Lynch and Liv Morgan, where Morgan captured the WWE Women’s World Championship.
items.raw_title: Stephanie Vaquer Cleared, Says She'll See Becky Lynch On Monday
items.src_summary: Stephanie Vaquer is ready to clash with Becky Lynch. On social media, Stephanie Vaquer revealed she is cleared and tossed her crutches to the ground. She said she would see Becky Lynch on Monday's WWE Raw.

items.title: Leon Slater Hopes For TNA Six-Sided Ring Return
items.summary: Leon Slater expressed his desire to wrestle in TNA's six-sided ring as the TNA World Champion. The British star, a longtime TNA fan, discussed the unique ring on the I Love Wrestling Podcast while reacting to the return of Destination X. He noted the six-sided ring was originally used from TNA's debut until 2010, revived in 2014 and retired again in 2018.
items.raw_title: Leon Slater Says He Would Love To Compete In TNA's Six-Sided Ring As TNA World Champion
items.src_summary: Leon Slater says he’d love to compete in a six-sided ring in TNA. When TNA first made its debut, they didn’t use the traditional four-sided ring but rather a six-sided wrestling ring, which was used until 2010. They later brought it back in 2014 but ultimately retired it again in 2018.

kind.quote: I would love the chance to be TNA World Champion and wrestle in a TNA six-sided ring.

updates.line: He made it clear he has no inside information about whether the six-sided ring is actually coming back.
updates.title: Leon Slater Wants TNA to Bring Back Six-Sided Ring for Destination X

items.title: Billy Gunn Recalls Unexpected AEW In-Ring Run
items.summary: Billy Gunn signed with AEW expecting to wrestle only about a dozen times per year while also working backstage. Instead he ended up competing frequently on both shows and capturing the AEW World Trios Championship with The Acclaimed as part of his "Daddy Ass" persona. On Inside The Ropes, Gunn said he was surprised by the career resurgence in his late 50s and early 60s but credited staying in shape for his ability to keep up with much younger opponents.
items.raw_title: Billy Gunn Says He Wrestled Much More Than Expected In AEW
items.src_summary: When Billy Gunn started with AEW, he expected to mainly be a coach while wrestling a handful of matches each year, but that quickly expanded.

kind.quote: Yeah, so my contract, I had 12 dates a year. Like, I really wasn't gonna wrestle, but I told Tony [Khan], 'If you need me to, I'll do some here and here and there.'

items.title: MVP Denies Hurt Syndicate Refusal To Put Talent Over

items.title: The Miz Recalls Early Locker Room Backlash After First WWE Tag Title Victory
items.summary: The Miz explained on WWE Vault that he and John Morrison drew heat from the locker room on the night they captured their first WWE tag team championships. After cutting loose on commentary during an ECW taping that preceded SmackDown, the duo was instructed to celebrate wildly upon winning the titles, which clashed with the planned focus on the opposing team. This excitement, especially as it marked Miz's initial WWE gold, further upset veterans who already viewed his Tough Enough background skeptically.
items.raw_title: The Miz Recalls Upsetting WWE Locker Room On The Day Of First Tag Title Win
items.src_summary: Among the many issues between The Miz and the WWE locker room early in his career, the wrestler recalled "ruffling feathers" on the night he won the tag title.

kind.quote: We used to shoot 'ECW' before 'SmackDown,' and so me and John Morrison went on ECW — I think it was a CM Punk match — and we went on commentary and we just ripped it apart, and people were upset about that.

items.title: Zack Sabre Jr. Refuses To Claim TMDK Leadership
items.summary: Zack Sabre Jr. says it is more fulfilling to watch members of TMDK thrive rather than position himself as the group's leader. He credits Shane Haste and Mikey Nicholls with founding TMDK in Australia in 2006 or 2007 and insists the faction belongs to Australian wrestling. The New Japan Pro-Wrestling branch features Sabre Jr., Robbie Eagles, Kosei Fujita, Ryohei Oiwa, Bad Dude Tito and Hartley Jackson, while Haste and Nicholls are set to reunite in Pro Wrestling NOAH on October 25.

kind.quote: I would never claim to be the leader of T.M.D.K., because it would never be mine.

items.title: Zack Sabre Jr. Recalls Shibata's 2021 NJPW Return Reaction
items.summary: During the 2021 G1 Climax, Zack Sabre Jr. faced Katsuyori Shibata in an exhibition match on day 19. Shibata had not appeared in NJPW since 2017. While appearing on CMLL’s Esto es Lucha Podcast, Sabre Jr. described the silent audience gasp when Shibata’s music hit under COVID restrictions as unlike anything he had experienced before and said it showed the power of pro wrestling.
items.raw_title: Zack Sabre Jr. Reflects On Exhibition Match Against Katsuyori Shibata, Says He's Never Experienced Anything Like That Reaction To Shibata
items.src_summary: Zack Sabre Jr. looks back on the exhibition. On day 19 of the 2021 New Japan Pro-Wrestling G1 Climax tournament, an exhibition match took place, and one of the participants was Zack Sabre Jr.

kind.quote: I’ve never experienced anything like the silent gasp of when the first bars of his theme music played where it was like, I felt in sync with the audience. That epitomized the power of pro wrestling.

items.title: Charlotte Flair Says Vulnerability Boosts Her Strength
items.summary: WWE star Charlotte Flair discussed the pressure of being Ric Flair's daughter and how it led to a decade as a villain with a disconnect from fans. After tearing her knee two years ago, she realized that embracing vulnerability makes her more powerful and resilient. This approach was the focus of her Player's Tribune article, allowing her to separate her on-screen character from real-life Ashley Fliehr and connect with audiences on a deeper level.
items.raw_title: WWE's Charlotte Flair: 'Being Vulnerable Makes You Powerful'
items.src_summary: WWE star Charlotte Flair opened up on how embracing vulnerability allowed her to connect with fans better.

kind.quote: Being vulnerable is what makes you powerful and resilient and strong

items.title: Iran Plots Against Americans Escalate Ahead of Crown Jewel
items.summary: U.S. intelligence officials warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Iranian efforts to target American personnel have reached advanced stages, according to The New York Times. The memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton notes a substantial increase in lethal plotting in the Middle East, Europe and elsewhere. The threat level against Americans is now assessed at its highest point since the war with Iran began in February, adding to security concerns for the upcoming Crown Jewel event in Riyadh.
items.raw_title: NYT: Iran in ‘advanced stages’ of planning attacks on Americans as Crown Jewel remains set for Riyadh
items.src_summary: U.S. intelligence officials have warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Iranian plans to attack Americans have reached “advanced stages,” according to The New York Times.

items.title: Leon Slater Says Option C Promo Made Him TNA's Top Guy
items.summary: Leon Slater defeated Cedric Alexander in a Last Man Standing Steel Cage match to win the TNA X Division Title at Lockdown. He then exercised Option C to challenge for Nic Nemeth's TNA World Title. Speaking on the I Love Wrestling Podcast, Slater said the Option C promo was the moment he transitioned from being seen as a kid to becoming the guy in TNA, with his Bound for Glory follow-up solidifying it further.
items.raw_title: Leon Slater Feels Like His Option C Promo At TNA Lockdown Was The Moment He Became 'The Guy' In TNA
items.src_summary: Leon Slater comments on his Option C promo at TNA Lockdown. On the show, Leon Slater competed in a Last Man Standing Steel Cage match for the TNA X Division Title. He defeated Cedric Alexander to become the new champion.

kind.quote: Yeah, absolutely. I think it’s rare that we get these pinpoint moments in wrestling. I’m not comparing here but just to use an analogy, the Austin 3:16 promo for example. You can point to that moment and you go, ‘Yeah, that’s when he became who he is.’ I feel like, for me, in my TNA run, the moment of me cashing in Option C was like, ‘Leon’s not the kid anymore. He is the guy now.’

items.title: Leon Slater Calls TNA World Title Reign Surreal
items.summary: Leon Slater became the youngest TNA World Champion in history after defeating Nic Nemeth at Bound for Glory, achieving the feat five years ahead of his own prediction. In a recent interview, the 22-year-old described how it took time to sink in that the title was his, noting he initially felt like he was carrying Nemeth's belt. Slater added that he still lives at home and recently had the championship on his TV table while playing GTA with friends, struggling to process the reality.
items.raw_title: Leon Slater Says TNA World Championship Is 'Finally Beginning To Feel Mine'
items.src_summary: Leon Slater comments on his TNA World Championship reign. At TNA Bound for Glory, Leon Slater defeated Nic Nemeth and became the youngest TNA World Champion in the company’s history. He accomplished his goal five years earlier than he predicted.

kind.quote: It feels very surreal, man. It took a while for it to settle in because I kind of felt like I was carrying Nic Nemeth’s belt around for a while just because I’ve so used to seeing him with it.

Per Fightful Select, he noted the venue has previously hosted WrestleMania and that Philadelphia has been one of AEW's strongest markets since the promotion launched. Remsburg believes the stadium would be in the conversation for a domestic All In but does not expect it to happen in 2027.
items.raw_title: Bryce Remsburg: If AEW Was Looking For A Domestic Stadium To Host All In, I Do Think Lincoln Financial Field Would Be In The Conversation
items.src_summary: Lincoln Financial Field hosting the event is a possibility. In September 2026, Fightful Select reported that the general feeling from those connected to AEW is that the 2027 installment of All In will take place in North America in some form.

kind.quote: if we were looking for a domestic stadium to host All In at, I do think The Linc would be in the conversation.

items.title: Kevin Nash Recalls Shawn Michaels Hospital Angle
items.summary: Kevin Nash pitched a detailed angle where Shawn Michaels sold a serious injury after taking a blow in a match. The plan involved both heels and babyfaces coming from the locker room to stand around Michaels before he was taken out on a stretcher. Nash said they checked Michaels into a Springfield hospital as part of the storyline, leading fans to call the facility seeking updates on his condition.
items.raw_title: Kevin Nash Remembers WWE's Shawn Michaels Checking Into Hospital To Sell A Storyline
items.src_summary: Hall of Famer Kevin Nash recalls how well Shawn Michaels did on selling a hospital visit for a WWE storyline.

kind.quote: I remember when we did the Shawn Michaels thing, when he took the blow and he went down, and I remember when I pitched it, I said, 'We can't have the commentators talk...We have to have the locker rooms come out, heels and babyfaces, kind of standing to make sure that he's f***ed, and then take him out...' I'm pretty sure we checked him into a Springfield hospital. So, people called. Shawn was in the hospital. So...you can make s*** real. But you can't make s*** half real.

kind.quote: In 2022, we really started going from Drew the Big Hero of Covid, the Scottish Warrior, to going down the path of becoming a bad guy.

items.title: Eric Bischoff Credits DDP's Authenticity For Getting Over In WCW
items.summary: On his "83 Weeks" podcast, WWE Hall of Famer Eric Bischoff disagreed with Diamond Dallas Page's belief that the Diamond Cutter finisher is what made him popular in WCW. Bischoff praised the move but said Page truly connected with fans when he dropped the larger-than-life character and became authentic as Page Falkinburg. Bischoff noted that Page's earlier gimmicks were forgettable and that being himself propelled him to the height of his popularity.
items.raw_title: WWE HOFer Eric Bischoff Disagrees With How Diamond Dallas Page Got Over In WCW
items.src_summary: According to Eric Bischoff, it was a simplification of Dallas Page's onscreen persona that won him over with fans, rather than his finishing move.

kind.quote: It's not what got him over. What got him over was when he became Page Falkinburg; when he allowed himself to go out and be authentic.

items.title: Michael Hayes Recalls Hiding From André The Giant
items.summary: While recounting his career, Michael Hayes described an incident where André the Giant was set to agent a show in Ohio featuring The Freebirds. After Hayes partied heavily the night before and needed to be carried into the building, the group later tried to avoid André at an airport by hiding behind a pillar. Hayes explained they were afraid because he had already been in trouble for showing up unprepared the first time André served as agent.
items.raw_title: Michael Hayes Recounts André The Giant Agenting Matches
items.src_summary: Michael Hayes discusses André. The latest episode of Stephanie McMahon's What's Your Story? podcast featured an extensive chat with WWE producer Michael Hayes. As they were going over Hayes' life and pro wrestling career, Hayes brought up that André the Giant agented matches.

kind.quote: We got up the next morning and there was a flight to New Haven or something and there was a flight to Atlanta, and it didn’t take long and all of a sudden, we’re changing our flights and here comes André, and we hid, all three of us are hiding behind this pillar, like, ‘I hope he don’t see us. Please don’t see us.’

updates.line: Michael Hayes revealed that Vince McMahon initially hated him and swore he would never work for WWE.

items.title: WWE Signs Four New Developmental Talents
items.summary: Per Fightful, Gabriela Martinez Asensi, Silvia Likki, Elly Finch and Tayleigh Robertson have all signed developmental contracts with WWE. Martinez Asensi is a Spanish tennis player and fitness coach from the University of Missouri, while Finch is a former University of Michigan shot putter whose signing was previously reported by PWInsider. items.title: WWE NXT Ratings Drop Against NBA Opener
items.summary: This week's WWE NXT on The CW drew 655,000 viewers, a 10.5 percent decline from the prior week's 732,000 and marking the third-lowest audience since late August. The 18-49 demographic rating fell to 0.10, down 28.6 percent week-over-week, as the show competed directly with the NBA regular season opener and NHL games. Year-over-year the numbers were still up, rising 24.8 percent in total viewers and 42.9 percent in the key demo against similar competition.

items.title: Swerve Strickland Claims Highest In-Ring Level For Black Wrestler
items.summary: AEW star Swerve Strickland told Billboard that his wrestling success stems purely from his in-ring performances rather than any agenda or persona. He stated that future generations will recognize him for performing at the highest level of any Black wrestler in history. Strickland noted past Black stars like The Rock and Booker T became household names but were rarely the best wrestlers on their shows due to the competition they faced.
items.raw_title: AEW's Swerve Strickland: I Perform At 'Highest Level' For A Black Wrestler In History
items.src_summary: AEW's Swerve Strickland told Billboard that he feels that he performs at the "highest level" you could see in pro wrestling history for a Black star.

kind.quote: I'm being me. My success in pro-wrestling is genuinely because of my ability in the ring. It's not because they're trying to push an agenda, it's because I perform at a really, really high level — probably the highest level you could see of a Black wrestler in the history of the game.

items.title: Dispensa Lawsuit Against AEW and Moxley Stays in Michigan
items.summary: A judge ruled that Christopher Dispensa's lawsuit against AEW and Jon Moxley will remain in Michigan. Dispensa claims Moxley went off-script during a 2023 match at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit and shoved him, causing injuries that led to cervical spine and shoulder surgery. The court determined that the incident location, witnesses and arena in Detroit made Michigan the proper venue, noting remote testimony options for Florida-based medical witnesses and that Michigan law would apply to the in-state injury.

items.title: Grayson Waller Shares Shawn Michaels' Reaction To NXT Pipebomb
items.summary: Grayson Waller returned to WWE NXT in July 2026 and delivered a shoot-style pipebomb promo that criticized the young roster. Speaking on Notsam Wrestling, Waller recalled telling Shawn Michaels beforehand that he hoped someone would confront him, to which Michaels replied he hoped one of the kids would slap him. Waller explained the goal was to test whether the NXT wrestlers had any fight in them after he eviscerated them on the mic, noting it became awkward backstage with no one saying anything to him.

kind.quote: And it’s funny because I said to Shawn [Michaels] before I went out, ‘I hope one of these kids comes and says something to me. That’s what we want.’ And Shawn said, ‘I hope one of these kids slaps you.’ And he meant that.

items.summary: Former AEW World Champion Swerve Strickland believes a co-promoted event between WWE and AEW is impossible. items.title: Erik and Sarah Logan Welcome Third Child
items.summary: Erik of the War Raiders announced the birth of his third child, a daughter named Dena, sharing a photo of himself holding the newborn. Both mother and baby are healthy. Erik and former WWE star Sarah Logan, who married in a Viking ceremony in 2018, already have two sons: Raymond born in February 2021 and Ezekiel born in November 2024. Logan left wrestling after her WWE contract expired in 2025 to focus on homesteading, farming and motherhood, while Erik recovered from 2023 neck surgery to win AAA tag titles in May 2025 and the WWE World Tag Team Championships with Ivar in December 2024 for a 124-day reign.

items.title: Saudi Airport Attack Kills One Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
items.summary: King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was hit on Wednesday night, resulting in one death and eight injuries along with property damage according to the General Authority of Civil Aviation. The eastern Saudi city has seen multiple attacks in recent weeks claimed by the Iran-backed Houthis, coming days before Riyadh hosts Canelo Alvarez versus Christian Mbilli on October 31 and WWE Crown Jewel the following week. Riyadh International Airport has faced heavy restrictions after prior incidents including one that killed 13 and injured over 300.
items.raw_title: Saudi government reports 1 dead, 8 injured following attack on Dammam airport
items.src_summary: An airport in Dammam was attacked on Wednesday night, Saudi Arabia's aviation authority confirmed in a statement.

items.title: WWE Licenses Brand for Online Casino Games
items.summary: WWE has entered the online casino market through multiple licensing partnerships. The company signed an exclusive multi-year deal with Fanatics Betting and Gaming in July 2025 to create WWE-themed online casino games for the US market. In January 2026 VGW secured rights to use the WWE brand for its online social games, allowing WWE to earn fees without operating or developing the gaming products itself.

items.title: Dominik Mysterio Eyes Multiple WWE Titles
items.summary: Dominik Mysterio recently lost the AAA MEGA Championship to El Grand Americano at TripleMania. In a Bleacher Report interview, he discussed potential targets including the World Heavyweight Championship held by Roman Reigns, the WWE Title involving Sami Zayn and Kevin Owens, his former Intercontinental Championship and the tag team titles alongside JD.
items.raw_title: Dominik Mysterio Discusses Current Title Aspirations In WWE
items.src_summary: Dominik Mysterio has discussed the various championships in WWE and his chances if he chose to go after them, including tag titles. Since AAA TripleMania, Mysterio has been without a championship belt after losing the MEGA Championship to El Grand Americano at the event.

kind.quote: There’s a lot of things I’d like to get done. I got some beef with Roman. He tried to throw me out of the ring and end my career one time. Sami Zayn, on the other hand, we’ve got a lot of history with Sami and Kevin in The Judgment Day, so maybe there’s something over there with the WWE title on the line. Maybe I want my IC title back. Maybe I wanna go for the tag titles with JD, get him some gold too. Who knows? There’s a lot of things I’d like to get done, but we’re taking it one day at a time.

items.title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals When He Considered Leaving WWE
items.summary: Ilja Dragunov's WWE contract expired in August and he chose not to renew it before joining AEW, where he made his debut at WrestleDream. The former NXT UK and NXT Champion told Ariel Helwani he first started thinking about departing around April or even a month earlier, after his ACL recovery title reign ended and creative directions did not align with what he hoped for beyond championship stories. He emphasized that it did not affect his work ethic as he loves the business.
items.raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Shares When He Thought About Leaving WWE
items.src_summary: Ilja Dragunov officially departed WWE in August when his contract expired, and he decided not to renew his deal. Dragunov had been off WWE TV since April when he competed in the Andre The Giant Memorial Battle Royal. He joined AEW after his deal expired, making his debut at AEW WrestleDream.

kind.quote: After I tore my ACL, I was fortunate to win a championship straight back on my comeback, which was an amazing moment for me that I still cherish. After I dropped the belt, things went into directions where I feel like it could’ve been better and more time to go into a story or something outside of holding a championship. Around April, maybe even a month before that, I was already just thinking about it.

The comments come from a recent interview reported by Fightful Select.
items.raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Says That The Expressive Part Of Wrestling Is 'The Real Exhausting Part'

kind.quote: It is definitely the part of expressing yourself. It is the vocality. It is the expressions. This part of portraying what you’re doing is at times much harder than any move that you can do.

items.title: Jaxson Ryker details severe injuries after WWE exit
items.summary: Former WWE star Jaxson Ryker discussed his 2023 retirement from wrestling, citing a neck injury and lower-back injury that caused arm and hand numbness along with extreme pain. He noted that his body was in bad shape following his 2021 WWE release, which led him to pursue other opportunities rather than continue. Ryker said he had long planned to walk away if wrestling stopped being enjoyable or his body hurt too badly, and he made a brief independent run before retiring.
items.raw_title: Former WWE star reveals ‘excruciating pain’ after release and lower back injury that caused arm numbness
items.src_summary: Former WWE star Jaxson Ryker opened up about his decision to step away from wrestling, revealing the persistent injuries and body aches that contributed to it. Ryker emphasized the toll of wrestling on his body following his WWE release in 2021.

kind.quote: My body, when I got released from WWE, my body was hurting real bad. I’d had a neck injury and a lower-back injury that was causing some numbness in my arm and my hand. Just really, really excruciating pain for the most part.

kind.quote: This entrance already meant the world for me. The music that I had is the music that I had in the beginning of my career. items.title: AJ Francis Praises Carlos Silva's TNA Leadership
items.summary: AJ Francis told The Wrestling Classic that Carlos Silva has a modern, sports-like leadership style in TNA that acknowledges talent right in front of him. Francis noted it has been nearly two years since he last held a championship in the promotion and said Silva recognizes that fact unlike previous regimes. He contrasted Silva's approach with the old wrestling style of ignoring established performers in favor of pushing newer ones.
items.raw_title: Former WWE star says Carlos Silva recognizes his value amid two-year TNA championship absence
items.src_summary: AJ Francis praised Carlos Silva’s leadership capabilities in TNA while expressing he knows his value and contributions to the promotion. Speaking with Justin Dhillon of The Wrestling Classic, Francis discussed the change in TNA’s leadership style with Silva at the helm.

kind.quote: His leadership style is more so of real sports. He doesn’t ignore what’s right in front of his face.

items.summary: Jeff Jarrett discussed the use of comedy in pro wrestling during an appearance reported by the Wrestling Observer. He explained that crowd reaction determines whether a comedic spot works and noted that creative decisions are subjective. Jarrett pointed to Mick Foley as an example of someone who could execute comedy effectively while maintaining seriousness when needed.

kind.quote: I mean, funny, don’t draw money is such a situational [concept]. I just don’t think you can paint it as…look, creative is subjective. Did you hear the reaction? They [the crowd] loved it.

items.title: Ilja Dragunov Discusses Ongoing Panic Attacks in Matches
items.summary: Ilja Dragunov told Ariel Helwani that he experiences panic attacks during wrestling matches on a regular basis. He explained that while he once tried to eliminate them, he now accepts the feeling as part of his life because it also drives him to perform with greater intensity, effort and love for the work. Dragunov added that the attacks happen multiple times per week but he no longer focuses on them.
items.raw_title: Ilja Dragunov opens up about experiencing panic attacks during wrestling matches
items.src_summary: Ilja Dragunov recently revealed that suffering panic attacks during his wrestling matches has become a consistent occurrence in his career. Recently, speaking to Ariel Helwani on The Ariel Helwani Show, Dragunov opened up about his experience with panic attacks. “I still have that.

kind.quote: I still have that. Sometimes I have this very bad, sometimes I have it less, but it’s a consistent thing that is kind of a part of my life.

items.title: Roman Reigns Shares Advice For Young WWE Talent

items.title: Will Ospreay Says Wrestling Has Evolved Past Full Kayfabe
items.summary: Will Ospreay believes professional wrestling in 2026 has moved beyond the need for complete kayfabe protection. He pointed to shows like WWE: Unreal and AEW: All Access that explore backstage elements while noting some aspects still require safeguarding. Ospreay compared the experience to watching superhero films where audiences accept the story without demanding protection of the business.
items.raw_title: Will Ospreay Feels Wrestling As 'Evolved' Past Needing Full Kayfabe Protection

items.title: Judge lets WWE Ring Boys lawsuit proceed
items.summary: A federal judge in Maryland denied the latest motion to dismiss the child sexual abuse case filed by multiple plaintiffs against Vince McMahon, Linda McMahon, WWE, and TKO. The 26-page opinion upheld the constitutionality of the state's Child Victims Act of 2023, which removed statutes of limitations for childhood sexual abuse claims. The plaintiffs are represented by DiCello Levitt and Murphy, Falcon & Murphy.

items.title: Mike Bailey Reveals Origin of MVP Feud Rumors
items.summary: Per the Wrestling Observer, Mike Bailey recently explained how online rumors of a backstage feud between himself and AEW's MVP began nearly a year ago. Bailey told The Wrestling Classic that both he and MVP saw the same fabricated story and reacted with disbelief, noting the absurdity since he and Kevin Knight had just faced MVP's group in an AEW World Tag Team Championship match at All In. items.title: AEW Dynamite Viewership Rises 44 Percent
items.summary: Dynamite drew 714,000 viewers and a 0.14 rating in the 18-49 demographic after returning to its regular timeslot, up from the previous week's numbers but below the four-week average. items.title: Cody Rhodes Names His Favorite Dusty Promo
items.summary: Cody Rhodes revealed that his favorite Dusty Rhodes promo is not the widely celebrated "Hard Times" but rather a 1994 WCW segment with brother Dustin titled "The View Never Changes." In it Dusty addressed neglecting Dustin and expressed a desire to become his tag team partner. Cody explained that the family has lived much of their story publicly and that the heartfelt promo served as Dusty's way of apologizing and saying he loved his son.
items.raw_title: WWE's Cody Rhodes Says His Favorite Dusty Rhodes Promo Isn't 'Hard Times'
items.src_summary: WWE star Cody Rhodes recalled his favorite promo cut by his father, Dusty Rhodes, and said it wasn't his dad's famous "Hard Times" segment.

kind.quote: My favorite promo he ever did was with my brother, Dustin, 'The View Never Changes,' talking about neglecting Dustin and wanting to be his partner.

items.title: Penta Recalls Stress Before Roman Reigns Bout
items.summary: Penta felt overwhelmed in the hours leading up to his match against Roman Reigns on the September 14 episode of WWE Raw in Mexico City. The luchador dealt with family being present, a complicated horse entrance that faced last-minute issues, makeup, an interview, a meet and greet, and the pressure of facing Reigns for the first time. In an interview with Busted Open Radio, Penta said he only began to process the experience two days afterward while sitting in his garden.
items.raw_title: Penta Recalls Stressful Day Leading Up To Roman Reigns Match
items.src_summary: Penta was quite stressed out before his match with Roman Reigns. The bout between Penta and Reigns took place on the September 14 edition of WWE Raw. Despite his loss, fans argue that Penta emerged from the match as a new main event player for WWE.

items.title: Anthony Bowens Explains His Post-Acclaimed AEW Storyline
items.summary: Anthony Bowens discussed his character arc after the Acclaimed's run in AEW. He noted the return was intentionally structured to lead into his heel turn where he blamed Billy Gunn and the fans while developing the Pride of Pro Wrestling persona. Bowens added that he channeled real emotions into the role and is currently aligned with The Opps.
items.raw_title: Anthony Bowens Says Everything After AEW Acclaimed Run Happened How It Was Supposed To

kind.quote: They think the return was a flop, which it wasn't. It was made to be that way so I could go off the deep end, blame Billy for my not being able to win the big matches, blame the fans for choosing Caster over me, adding to his delusion of being the best wrestler alive. And then I would go into what the Pride of Pro Wrestling was.

items.title: William Regal Urges Wrestlers To Sell Pins And Kickouts Better
items.summary: WWE veteran William Regal advised wrestlers to treat every pin attempt and kick-out with maximum intensity as if their career depended on it. He pointed to an early 2000s match between AJ Styles and Amazing Red as the ideal example where both men covered shoulders fully and exploded out with force. Regal stressed that this approach respects the audience's time and maintains the realism of the pro wrestling story.
items.raw_title: WWE's William Regal: Wrestlers Should Pay More Attention To Pin Attempts & Kick-Outs
items.src_summary: 42-year industry veteran William Regal offers valuable advice about wrestling pin attempts and kick-outs.

kind.quote: We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts. If you don't win you would make less money in the story we're telling. Please pin and kick out like your life and career depend on it.

items.title: Cody Rhodes Links Neck Tattoo To Career Rise
items.summary: Cody Rhodes got his neck tattoo after leaving New Japan Pro-Wrestling's Bullet Club because he wanted his own distinct logo instead of the faction's gun design. The American Nightmare logo draws from the Street Fighter villain M. Bison and Shadaloo, an idea he gave the artist after seeing it in a Burlesque Hall scene. Rhodes debuted the tattoo at AEW Revolution 2020, returned to WWE in 2022, and has held the Undisputed WWE Championship three times since.

items.title: Cena Ate Hornswoggle's Vomit-Covered Burger After Missed Flight
items.summary: John Cena, Christian Cage and Hornswoggle were stranded in Ireland due to a volcano preventing their return for a WWE Raw episode. After a night of heavy drinking, Hornswoggle vomited on his room service hamburger, which Christian placed in the hallway after putting him to bed. Hours later a hungry Cena found the untouched-looking burger and ate it, only learning the truth from the pair the next morning.
items.raw_title: A Missed WWE Flight In Ireland Led To Hornswoggle Vomiting On John Cena's Hamburger
items.src_summary: Having an incredible WWE career, the "Never Seen 17" star John Cena recalls an unforgettable night that did not end in his favor.

kind.quote: We got stuck in Ireland because there was a volcano and we couldn't get back to the states to perform [on] '[WWE] Raw.'

items.title: Austin Creed Feels Revitalized In AEW
items.summary: Austin Creed discussed his thoughts about potentially joining AEW during his WWE tenure. Two months after arriving at All In with Kofi as The New Level, they teamed with Swerve Strickland to win the AEW World Trios Championship. Creed praised the environment, noting the passionate fans and how the energy allows performers to elevate their game.

kind.quote: For me and Kof, we’re just revitalized.

items.title: Dominik Mysterio Skips NXT Training For Main Roster
items.summary: Dominik Mysterio explained that he never attended WWE Performance Center classes because his schedule with Raw, NXT and SmackDown left no room for them on Wednesdays. He learned on the job instead by working live events and television with main roster talent. Mysterio later joined NXT after already competing on the main roster and captured the NXT North American Championship in his second match there, holding it for over two months.
items.raw_title: Dominik Mysterio Explains Why He Bypassed Full WWE NXT Run
items.src_summary: Dominik Mysterio has explained why he skipped NXT when he began his full-time WWE career and how he learned on the job while on the main roster.

kind.quote: At that point, I didn't see what I was going to learn when I was learning from everyone on the road doing three different TV shows.

items.title: Chad Gable Remembers WWE Match Against Kurt Angle
items.summary: Chad Gable described his match with Kurt Angle on Monday Night Raw as a dream come true. The bout took place in Chicago near his home state of Minnesota and the pair were given extra time in a rare occurrence under Vince McMahon's era allowing them to wrestle on the fly. Gable said it was a wonderful night except for receiving a speeding ticket on the drive home.
items.raw_title: Chad Gable Recalls WWE Match With Kurt Angle, Getting Pulled Over Afterwards
items.src_summary: WWE Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable recalls his lone singles match with Kurt Angle in 2019, revealing that he was pulled over for speeding after

kind.quote: The cool thing I do remember about that is, in a very rare occurrence on a 'Monday Night Raw' live, we actually ended up getting more time than we were supposed to, in the moment. So we just got to wrestle. And to be able to just go in there and just be wrestling on the fly, winging it with Kurt Angle of all people, it's like 'This is happening?' And this is in Chicago, which is great, the crowd is always great. It was a great night man, except I got a speeding ticket on the way home.

items.title: Will Ospreay Would Run Underground Wrestling If Banned
items.summary: Will Ospreay told WKMG News 6 that he is extremely grateful for his current spot in pro wrestling. The AEW star recalled starting out wrestling in his backyard on a trampoline and in other backyard promotions before receiving formal training. Ospreay added that his passion is so strong that if wrestling were made illegal he would continue by running a secret mafia-style underground promotion.
items.raw_title: Will Ospreay: If Wrestling Became Illegal Tomorrow, I'd Be Like The Criminal Mastermind Of An Underground Mafia Wrestling Promotion
items.src_summary: Will Ospreay discusses his adoration for the pro wrestling industry, noting how far he would go to remain a pro wrestler.

kind.quote: I’m so blessed to be able to be in this position, to be able to just do something that… I love doing, like I’ve said it so many times, if wrestling became like illegal tomorrow, like I’d be in my garden wrestling. Like I’d happily, like I’d be like the criminal mastermind of like an underground, Mafia wrestling run promotion.

items.title: Matt Hardy Breaks Down Tiffany Stratton Ladder Mishap
items.summary: Matt Hardy analyzed Tiffany Stratton's Swanton bomb attempt from the top of a tall ladder during the women's Money in the Bank ladder match. items.title: Will Ospreay Grateful For Kicking Out Of One Winged Angel
items.summary: Will Ospreay faced Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship at All In this past August in England. Ospreay kicked out of Omega's protected One Winged Angel finisher during the match, a feat previously accomplished by only a small number of wrestlers including Kota Ibushi and Omega. In a recent interview, Ospreay expressed that earning Omega's trust with the moment elevated him to legendary status and left him extremely grateful.
items.raw_title: Will Ospreay On Kicking Out Of The One Winged Angel At AEW All In: To Have That Was Out Of This World And Mindblowing
items.src_summary: Will Ospreay reflects on kicking out of Kenny Omega's One Winged Angel at AEW All In 2026 back in August. At AEW's biggest pay-per-view of the year this past August, Will would challenge for the AEW World Championship against Kenny Omega in his home country of England.

kind.quote: That I won Kenny’s trust, because a lot of that comes down to how much he wants to protect it and going forward, like where… Where does that put me? It just elevates me up to like a legendary status that I will never fully be able to express my gratitude for having that type of moment with someone that I do generally look at as like a hero of mine. So to have that was just out of this world, mind blowing. Like I’m just super grateful for it.

items.title: Maria Kanellis Details 2017 WWE Return Path
items.summary: Maria Kanellis explained on Insight With Chris Van Vliet how the Laurel Van Ness wedding storyline in TNA drew WWE's attention to her and Mike Bennett. The pair had been working in Ring of Honor and New Japan through late 2015 when a call from writer David Lagana brought them to TNA with promises of a main storyline and creative control. They signed with WWE in June 2017 and returned at that year's Money in the Bank event, marking Kanellis' first appearance with the company since 2010.

items.summary: Nick Wayne defeated Chris Jericho in their third match at AEW WrestleDream on Saturday to earn his second victory over the veteran. Following their initial Dynamite meeting in September and their Grand Slam France encounter earlier this month, Wayne grabbed a microphone post-match to celebrate the win while Jericho recovered on the floor.

items.title: Adam Copeland Credits AEW For Historic Venue Run
items.summary: Adam Copeland shared that returning to WWE in 2020 made him doubt he'd ever wrestle in his dream venues like Arena Mexico, Wembley Stadium and the Tokyo Dome. After moving to AEW those opportunities opened up, allowing him to perform at Arena Mexico, Wembley Stadium and Maple Leaf Gardens all within one month. He said these bucket-list experiences are what keep him motivated and fired up during his current run.
items.raw_title: Adam Copeland Explains How Joining AEW Opened The Door To Historic Venues

kind.quote: Moving to AEW, then suddenly that became a possibility and now, within one calendar month, to be able to check off Arena Mexico, to be able to check off Wembley Stadium, and now to be able to do Maple Leaf Gardens? That, for me, is just amazing.

items.title: Keanu Carver Set For Court Hearing
items.summary: Keanu Carver, whose real name is Kevin Robertson, is scheduled to appear in Seminole County, Florida court on October 20 for a review of a protective order issued against him. The injunction, filed on September 14 and upheld on September 22, bars him from contacting an NXT talent amid allegations of stalking and domestic violence. items.title: Bandido Surpasses Jay Lethal For Most Combined ROH World Title Days
items.summary: Bandido broke Jay Lethal's record for the most overall days as ROH World Champion on October 14. Bandido's current reign, which began at AEW Dynasty in April 2025, stands at 558 days as he targets Samoa Joe's all-time single-reign record of 645 days.

items.title: Bully Ray Praises Je'Von Evans' Intense Ambulance Return
items.summary: Bully Ray highlighted a specific moment from the men's Money in the Bank ladder match that stood out more than Je'Von Evans' other spots. After being wheeled away, Evans returned in an ambulance, forcefully opened the door to knock Bron Breakker down, and unloaded with purposeful punches that Ray felt conveyed real intent and made him believe in Evans as a babyface. The WWE Hall of Famer emphasized that the convincing fist strikes and determination shown were more impactful than any other part of the match, proving less is more.

items.summary: Swerve Strickland convinced AEW's New Level to form a trio by highlighting the chance to immediately face six or seven top tag teams at Wembley. items.title: John Cena Explains Benefits of WWE's PG Era
items.summary: John Cena discussed WWE's shift to a PG rating during an appearance on What Now? With Trevor Noah. He noted the rebranding process took over a decade to gain acceptance and enabled the company to distribute content worldwide since many countries reject PG-13 or MA material. Cena also highlighted how the rise of social media and content creation around 2008 helped elevate wrestlers beyond their previous carny image, leading to massive audience engagement and influence for WWE.

kind.quote: Well, here’s the good thing about PG: you can ship it anywhere.

items.title: Drew McIntyre Slams Pre-Planned Matches
items.summary: WWE star Drew McIntyre criticized wrestlers who map out complete matches beforehand, preferring instead to discuss basics like match length then adapt to the live crowd reaction. He noted that rigidly choreographed bouts often fall flat when audiences respond differently than expected and said many performers today lack the ability to improvise on the fly. McIntyre stressed that panicking during a live broadcast creates an awkward and disjointed feel for everyone involved.
items.raw_title: Drew McIntyre criticizes wrestlers who plan entire matches in advance
items.src_summary: WWE’s Drew McIntyre says he can’t stand wrestlers who plan entire wrestling matches in advance. Speaking on Bradley Martyn’s Raw Talk, McIntyre opened up about his in-ring match psychology and how he prefers to listen to the crowd and perform.

kind.quote: I can’t stand when people plan stuff from beginning to end because you don’t know how the crowd’s going to react.

items.title: Kit Wilson Embraces Growth in WWE Singles Run
items.summary: After his Pretty Deadly partner Elton Prince suffered an injury and stepped away, Kit Wilson transitioned into a singles competitor and has formed an alliance with The Miz. In an interview Wilson described the shift from lifelong tag team wrestler to solo performer as a personal journey that forced him to address weaknesses previously covered by a partner. He stated the experience has helped him mature both as a man and in-ring talent, leaving him better than ever while focused on continued growth.
items.raw_title: Kit Wilson reflects on unexpected challenges of WWE singles career
items.src_summary: Ever since Pretty Deadly member Elton Prince got injured and went on a hiatus, Kit Wilson reinvented himself and emerged as a popular singles wrestler. Currently in a partnership with The Miz, Wilson recently opened up to Denice Salcedo, where he reflected on the challenges of a singles career.

kind.quote: It’s been finding myself. Sometimes art imitates life and life art, and as I go through this change on TV, going from a tag team wrestler- and I was only ever a tag team guy, and I was so committed to that- into this singles journey, it really grows you as a person and you kind of mature with it.

Gowen cited his 2025 one-off AEW match against Ricochet, with family at ringside, as the highlight of his career following his battle with drug addiction featured in Dark Side of the Ring.

items.title: Mike Bailey cherishes emotional Montreal homecoming

Bailey recalled standing atop the ladder and seeing familiar faces of relatives and close friends who had surprised him by showing up without telling him in advance.

items.title: Deonna Purrazzo Credits TNA Run For Building Her Confidence
items.summary: Deonna Purrazzo told The Ledgera that her years in TNA Wrestling shaped her more than any other period in her career. After joining in 2020 at a time when she considered leaving the business, she found a supportive environment that helped her win five world titles, main event multiple shows and lead a division while staying true to herself. The Virginia native previously worked for TNA from 2014-2017 before returning for a second stint that lasted until 2023.
items.raw_title: Deonna Purrazzo: ‘My Time In TNA Gave Me The Confidence To Know I Could Lead A Division And Do It Without Compromising Who I Am And What I Stood For’

kind.quote: My time in TNA/IMPACT shaped me the most.

items.title: Kaitlyn Recalls Unhappy 2014 WWE Exit
items.summary: Kaitlyn explained that her 2014 departure from WWE came after a difficult travel day to Baltimore, the same city where she had debuted years earlier. She was not booked for television, felt deeply unhappy, and asked for her release from Mark Carano in Talent Relations. Carano asked her to sleep on the decision before proceeding.
items.raw_title: Kaitlyn discusses WWE exit in 2014 : ‘I just wanted to be done’
items.src_summary: Former WWE star Kaitlyn opened up about the circumstances that led to her decision to part ways with the company in 2014. Kaitlyn recalled informing Mark Carano, the former VP of Talent Relations, about requesting for her WWE release.

kind.quote: I just wanted to be done

items.title: WWE upset over staff voicing Saudi travel fears
items.summary: WWE is unhappy that several non-wrestling employees have publicly expressed reluctance to travel to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel due to the current regional security situation. No wrestlers have commented on the matter, which the company views as maintaining a united front. WWE has an internal backup U.S. venue prepared if the event must be relocated but refuses to acknowledge it publicly to avoid upsetting Saudi officials.

items.summary: AEW has finalized the eight-man Clockwork Carnage bout for WrestleDream this Saturday where the winner will be crowned the new AEW World Champion. The participants are defending champion Will Ospreay, Samoa Joe, Speedball Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet and Darby Allin. The final five qualifiers were decided on Wednesday's Dynamite with Takeshita submitting Brian Cage, Okada pinning Myron Reed, Copeland pinning Josh Alexander, Ricochet pinning Ace Austin and Allin defeating Hechicero.

items.summary: CMLL World Heavyweight Champion Hechicero will battle Zack Sabre Jr. in a non-title singles match on the November 16 Lucha Kingdom co-promoted show from Arena Mexico in Mexico City. items.title: TNA Apologizes For Max Caster's Riyadh Comments
items.summary: TNA Wrestling issued a statement apologizing for Max Caster's unscripted insensitive remarks about deadly attacks in Riyadh during the Bound For Glory pay-per-view. The promotion accepted full responsibility for allowing the segment to air, removed it from all replays and social media, and confirmed Caster will no longer work with the company. The statement expressed condolences to victims and their families while promising preventive measures.

items.title: WWE ESPN Lawsuit Response Deadline Set
items.summary: A federal judge in Connecticut gave WWE, ESPN and related parties until October 16 to respond to an objection filed by plaintiffs Michael Diesa and Rebella Toback over adding ESPN and BAMTech as defendants. The objection concerns allegations that WWE misled buyers about accessing major events on the ESPN Unlimited platform after WrestlePalooza 2025. The court will delay any decision on moving the case to arbitration until the objection is resolved. The proposed class covers U.S. customers who paid for the ESPN App between August 6 and September 20 2025 while already subscribed through cable or live TV providers.

items.title: AJ Styles Reveals Reason He Rejected Bullet Club Leadership
items.summary: AJ Styles explained that he positioned Bullet Club as a group where no one followed a single leader so every member would remain equally important. He emphasized that the faction's appeal came from everyone working together rather than focusing on individual stars like himself, Karl Anderson or Doc Gallows. Styles added that the group's visible enjoyment of their time together helped boost their popularity with Japanese audiences before the stable's quiet disbandment in early 2026.
items.raw_title: WWE's AJ Styles Explains Why He Didn't Want To Be The 'Leader' Of Bullet Club In NJPW

kind.quote: We don't follow anybody, and so therefore that means you don't follow me. I'm not your leader, I'm just part of this group because we don't follow anybody.

items.title: Steven Borden Sacrifices Career For AEW Wrestling Dream
items.summary: AEW wrestler Steven Borden left his growing role managing a sports technology company to pursue a full-time pro wrestling career like his father Sting. One year after his debut, Borden has already reached AEW's main roster with guidance from Darby Allin. He described the difficult choice during an episode of AEW Close-Up, noting the intense 80-90 hour work weeks made it impossible to succeed at both.
